_meta.description: Curated adult reference intervals (fallback when the report does not print its own range), LOINC codes, unit conversions to a canonical unit, physiologic plausibility limits and critical (panic) limits.
_meta.notes: ranges = [low, high] in canonical unit; null means open-ended. conversions map a unit to a multiplicative factor into the canonical unit, or {a, b} for canonical = a*x + b. Ranges vary by lab, age, pregnancy and method; the range printed on the report always takes precedence.
_meta.sources: Common Indian lab reference intervals, Mayo Clinic Laboratories, ADA Standards of Care 2024 (glycemia), NCEP ATP III (lipids), KDIGO (eGFR), Endocrine Society (vitamin D).

tests.what: the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells
tests.low: can be seen with anaemia, for example from iron, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, blood loss or chronic illness
tests.high: can be seen with dehydration, smoking, living at high altitude or some lung, heart or bone-marrow conditions

tests.what: the number of red blood cells
tests.low: can be seen with anaemia or blood loss
tests.high: can be seen with dehydration or conditions where the body makes extra red cells

tests.what: the share of blood volume made up of red cells
tests.low: often moves together with low haemoglobin (anaemia)
tests.high: can be seen with dehydration

tests.what: the average size of red blood cells
tests.low: small red cells, which can be seen with iron deficiency or thalassaemia trait
tests.high: large red cells, which can be seen with vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol use or thyroid problems

tests.what: the average amount of haemoglobin in each red cell
tests.low: can be seen with iron deficiency
tests.high: can be seen with vitamin B12 or folate deficiency

tests.what: the concentration of haemoglobin inside red cells
tests.low: can be seen with iron deficiency
tests.high: is uncommon and is sometimes a sample or measurement effect

tests.what: how much red cells vary in size
tests.low: is usually not significant
tests.high: means red cells vary more in size, which can be seen with nutritional anaemias

tests.what: the number of white blood cells, which fight infection
tests.low: can be seen with some viral infections (such as dengue), certain medicines or bone-marrow problems
tests.high: can be seen with infections, inflammation, stress, steroid medicines or, less often, blood disorders

tests.what: the share of white cells that are neutrophils (fight bacteria)
tests.low: can be seen with some viral infections or medicines
tests.high: can be seen with bacterial infections, inflammation or stress

tests.what: the share of white cells that are lymphocytes (fight viruses)
tests.low: can be seen during acute illness or stress
tests.high: can be seen with viral infections

tests.what: the share of white cells that are monocytes
tests.low: is usually not significant on its own
tests.high: can be seen during recovery from infection or with chronic inflammation

tests.what: the share of white cells that are eosinophils
tests.low: is usually not significant
tests.high: can be seen with allergies, asthma or parasitic (worm) infections

tests.what: the share of white cells that are basophils
tests.low: is usually not significant
tests.high: can be seen with allergic reactions and, rarely, blood disorders

tests.what: cells that help blood clot
tests.low: can be seen with viral infections such as dengue, some medicines, liver disease or bone-marrow problems; very low counts raise bleeding risk
tests.high: can be seen with inflammation, iron deficiency or after bleeding

tests.what: a general marker of inflammation
tests.low: is usually not significant
tests.high: is a non-specific sign of inflammation or infection and rises with age and anaemia

tests.what: the sugar level in blood after at least 8 hours without food
tests.low: low sugar (hypoglycaemia) can cause shakiness, sweating or confusion and can happen with diabetes medicines
tests.high: 100-125 mg/dL is in the prediabetes range and 126 mg/dL or more (confirmed on repeat testing) is in the diabetes range

tests.what: blood sugar about 2 hours after a meal
tests.low: low sugar can happen with diabetes medicines
tests.high: 140-199 mg/dL can suggest impaired glucose tolerance and 200 mg/dL or more is in the diabetes range

tests.what: blood sugar at any time of day
tests.low: low sugar can happen with diabetes medicines or skipped meals
tests.high: 200 mg/dL or more with symptoms such as thirst and frequent urination is in the diabetes range

tests.what: the average blood sugar over the last 2-3 months
tests.low: is uncommon and can be affected by anaemia or blood loss
tests.high: 5.7-6.4% is in the prediabetes range and 6.5% or more is in the diabetes range; for people already treated for diabetes, the doctor sets an individual target

tests.what: the total amount of cholesterol in blood
tests.low: is usually not a concern
tests.high: 200-239 mg/dL is borderline high and 240 mg/dL or more is high, which over time raises heart and blood-vessel risk

tests.what: a type of fat in blood, affected by diet, alcohol and sugar levels
tests.low: is usually not a concern
tests.high: 150-199 mg/dL is borderline and higher values add to heart risk; very high values (500 mg/dL or more) can inflame the pancreas

tests.what: 'good' cholesterol that helps remove cholesterol from blood vessels
tests.low: low HDL is linked to higher heart risk; exercise and not smoking can help raise it
tests.high: is generally considered favourable

tests.what: 'bad' cholesterol that can build up in blood vessels
tests.low: is generally considered favourable
tests.high: 100-129 mg/dL is above the optimal level, 130-159 mg/dL is borderline high and 160 mg/dL or more is high; people with diabetes or heart disease are often given lower targets by their doctor

tests.what: a cholesterol carrier usually calculated from triglycerides
tests.low: is usually not a concern
tests.high: usually rises along with triglycerides

tests.what: a waste product cleared by the kidneys
tests.low: can be seen with low protein intake or liver conditions
tests.high: can be seen with dehydration, a high-protein diet or reduced kidney function

tests.what: a waste product cleared by the kidneys
tests.low: can be seen with low protein intake
tests.high: can be seen with dehydration or reduced kidney function

tests.what: a waste product from muscles that reflects how well the kidneys filter
tests.low: can be seen with low muscle mass
tests.high: can mean the kidneys are filtering less well; dehydration and some medicines can also raise it

tests.what: an estimate of how well the kidneys filter blood
tests.low: 60-89 is mildly reduced, and below 60 for 3 months or more suggests chronic kidney disease
tests.high: is generally not a concern

tests.what: a waste product from the breakdown of purines in food
tests.low: is usually not significant
tests.high: can be linked to gout or kidney stones and is affected by diet, alcohol and some medicines

tests.what: a salt that controls fluid balance
tests.low: can be seen with vomiting, diarrhoea, some medicines (such as diuretics) or drinking very large amounts of water
tests.high: usually reflects dehydration

tests.what: a mineral important for heart rhythm and muscles
tests.low: can be seen with vomiting, diarrhoea or some diuretic medicines
tests.high: can be seen with kidney problems or some blood-pressure medicines; very high levels can affect heart rhythm

tests.what: a salt that works with sodium to balance fluids
tests.low: can be seen with vomiting
tests.high: can be seen with dehydration or diarrhoea

tests.what: a mineral for bones, muscles and nerves
tests.low: can be seen with low vitamin D or low albumin
tests.high: can be seen with parathyroid problems, excess supplements or some other conditions

tests.what: a yellow pigment processed by the liver
tests.low: is not a concern
tests.high: can cause yellowing of eyes or skin (jaundice) and can be seen with liver conditions, gallbladder blockage, faster red-cell breakdown or harmless Gilbert syndrome

tests.what: bilirubin already processed by the liver
tests.low: is not a concern
tests.high: can be seen with liver conditions or a blockage of bile flow

tests.what: an enzyme found in the liver, heart and muscles
tests.low: is not a concern
tests.high: can be seen with liver inflammation (fatty liver, hepatitis, alcohol, some medicines) or muscle injury

tests.what: an enzyme found mainly in the liver
tests.low: is not a concern
tests.high: can be seen with liver inflammation, for example fatty liver, viral hepatitis, alcohol or some medicines

tests.what: an enzyme from the liver and bones
tests.low: is uncommon and can be seen with some nutritional deficiencies
tests.high: can be seen with bile-flow problems, bone growth or bone conditions, and pregnancy

tests.what: a liver enzyme sensitive to alcohol and bile-flow problems
tests.low: is not a concern
tests.high: can be seen with alcohol use, fatty liver, bile-flow problems or some medicines

tests.what: the total protein in blood
tests.low: can be seen with poor nutrition, liver or kidney conditions
tests.high: can be seen with dehydration or chronic inflammation

tests.what: the main protein made by the liver
tests.low: can be seen with poor nutrition, liver disease, kidney protein loss or illness
tests.high: usually reflects dehydration

tests.what: proteins including antibodies
tests.low: can be seen with some immune or liver conditions
tests.high: can be seen with chronic infections or inflammation

tests.what: a hormone from the brain that tells the thyroid how hard to work
tests.low: can suggest an overactive thyroid or too high a dose of thyroid medicine
tests.high: can suggest an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism) or too low a dose of thyroid medicine

tests.what: an active thyroid hormone
tests.low: can be seen with an underactive thyroid or during illness
tests.high: can be seen with an overactive thyroid

tests.what: the main hormone made by the thyroid
tests.low: can be seen with an underactive thyroid
tests.high: can be seen with an overactive thyroid

tests.what: the unbound, active form of thyroxine
tests.low: can be seen with an underactive thyroid
tests.high: can be seen with an overactive thyroid or too much thyroid medicine

tests.what: a vitamin important for bones and muscles
tests.low: 20-29 ng/mL is often called insufficient and below 20 ng/mL deficient; it is common in India and usually treated with supplements and sunlight as advised by a doctor
tests.high: very high levels usually come from too many supplements

tests.what: a vitamin needed for nerves and making red blood cells
tests.low: can cause tiredness, tingling or anaemia; it is more common with vegetarian diets and long-term metformin or antacid use
tests.high: usually reflects supplements

tests.what: the body's iron stores
tests.low: suggests low iron stores (iron deficiency)
tests.high: can be seen with inflammation, infection, liver conditions or iron overload

tests.what: the amount of iron circulating in blood
tests.low: can be seen with iron deficiency or inflammation
tests.high: can be seen with iron supplements or iron overload

tests.what: a protein that rises with inflammation or infection
tests.low: is normal
tests.high: is a non-specific sign of infection or inflammation

tests.what: the pressure in arteries when the heart beats (top number)
tests.low: can cause dizziness and can be seen with dehydration or medicines
tests.high: 120-129 is elevated and 130 or more on repeated readings is in the high blood pressure range; 180 or more needs prompt medical attention

tests.what: the pressure in arteries between heartbeats (bottom number)
tests.low: can be seen with dehydration or medicines
tests.high: 80 or more on repeated readings is in the high blood pressure range

tests.what: heartbeats per minute
tests.low: can be normal in fit people or caused by some medicines
tests.high: can be seen with fever, pain, dehydration, anxiety or heart rhythm problems

tests.what: how much oxygen the blood is carrying
tests.low: below 94% can mean the lungs or heart need attention, and below 90% needs urgent care
tests.high: is not a concern

tests.what: body temperature
tests.low: can be seen with exposure to cold
tests.high: fever, usually from infection

tests.what: body weight
height
weight relative to height
tests.low: below 18.5 is underweight
tests.high: 25-29.9 is overweight and 30 or more is obesity (for Asian Indians, lower cut-offs of 23 and 25 are often used)

tests.what: breaths per minute
tests.low: can be seen with some medicines or drowsiness
tests.high: can be seen with fever, lung problems or anxiety
